reasoning: Taller forest with more variable structure was expected to offer more nest platforms and overhead cover. In Desolation Sound, predicted suitability rose with vertical complexity, and earlier ground studies had linked murrelets to vertically complex forest. Ground plots at Clayoquot Sound nests found shorter and less varied canopy than at random sites, so the direction was contested there.

Gaps within and under the canopy were expected to give flight access to nests. In Desolation Sound, however, predicted suitability fell as internal gaps increased. On the south coast, an air photo model placed nests where small gaps were sporadic but large gaps occurred. Small gaps had nonetheless been reported beside nest trees and at all 7 nest patches studied on Haida Gwaii. In Washington and on southwest Vancouver Island, nest sites were more open than nearby forest.
